scenes.title: A New Queen
beats: Long ago, many of God’s people lived far from home, in the great land of Persia. A girl named Esther lived there. She had no mom or dad, so her kind cousin Mordecai raised her as his very own daughter.
One day, the great King Xerxes was looking for a new queen. Of all the young women in the whole kingdom, the king loved Esther the most!
So the king set a royal crown on Esther’s head, and she became the queen. But Mordecai told her, “Don’t tell anyone yet that you are one of God’s people.”

layers.prompt: A full-bleed painting: the scene itself reaches all four edges of the picture, one continuous view: in a grand Persian palace hall with tall carved columns, colorful tiles and silk curtains in warm golden light: King Xerxes gently sets a golden crown on Esther’s head as she bows her head with a shy smile, right of center, while courtiers and maids watch happily and Mordecai peeks in proudly from a doorway

scenes.title: Haman’s Wicked Plan
beats: The king had a proud helper named Haman. The king made a rule: everyone had to bow down to Haman. And everyone did, except for Mordecai.
Mordecai would only bow down to God. That made Haman so angry that his face turned red!
So Haman tricked the king into making a terrible law: on one day, all of God’s people would be destroyed. And the king didn’t even know that his own queen was one of them!

layers.prompt: A full-bleed painting: the scene itself reaches all four edges of the picture, one continuous view: at the big stone gate of the Persian palace in the bright afternoon: proud Haman in his tall hat struts past, nose in the air, while a row of people bow low to him, but Mordecai stands tall right of center with his arms folded calmly, not bowing, and Haman glares at him with a furious red face

scenes.title: For Such a Time as This
beats: Mordecai sent Queen Esther a message: “You must ask the king to save our people! Who knows? Maybe God made you queen for just such a time as this.”
But there was a rule. Anyone who went to the king without being called could be put to death, unless the king held out his golden scepter.
Esther was scared, but she was brave. “Pray for me for three days,” she said. “Then I will go to the king, even though it is against the rule.”

layers.prompt: A full-bleed painting: the scene itself reaches all four edges of the picture, one continuous view: in Queen Esther’s room in the palace at night, lit by little oil lamps and moonlight through an arched window: Esther kneels on a rug right of center, praying with her hands folded and her eyes closed, while her maids kneel and pray quietly around her

scenes.title: The Golden Scepter
beats: On the third day, Esther put on her royal robes and walked into the king’s throne room. Everyone held their breath. Would the king be angry?
The king looked at Esther, and he smiled! He held out his golden scepter, and Esther touched the tip of it.
“What is it, Queen Esther?” said the king. “Whatever you ask, I will give it to you, even half of my kingdom!”

layers.prompt: A full-bleed painting: the scene itself reaches all four edges of the picture, one continuous view: in the king’s magnificent throne room with blue-and-gold tiles, tall columns and a high golden throne on steps: King Xerxes sits on the throne right of center looking surprised, while Esther in her royal robes stands bravely at the foot of the steps, and guards and servants watch nervously

scenes.title: Esther Speaks Up
beats: Esther invited the king and Haman to a special feast. Then she said, “O king, please save my life, and the lives of my people! Someone wants to destroy us all.”
“Who would dare to do such a thing?” asked the king. Esther pointed. “It is this wicked man, Haman!”
The king was very angry with Haman, and Haman was punished for his wicked plan. Then the king gave Mordecai Haman’s important job instead!

layers.prompt: A full-bleed painting: the scene itself reaches all four edges of the picture, one continuous view: at a royal feast in a beautiful palace garden room with a long low table full of fruit, bread and golden cups, under hanging lanterns: Queen Esther, King Xerxes and Haman recline on cushions around the table, right of center, Haman smugly sipping from a golden cup

layers.hint: Tap to hear Esther speak up
layers.edit: Queen Esther now stands up tall and bravely points straight at Haman; King Xerxes has risen to his feet with an angry frown, and Haman shrinks back in fright, dropping his golden cup with a clatter.

scenes.title: From Sad to Glad
beats: The king made a new law so God’s people could protect themselves. And Mordecai came out of the palace in royal robes of blue and white, with a golden crown!
In every city, God’s people sang and danced and feasted. Their sadness had turned to joy!
God never stopped taking care of His people, even when they were far from home. And every year, they still have a happy party called Purim to remember how God saved them, through one brave queen.

layers.prompt: A full-bleed painting: the scene itself reaches all four edges of the picture, one continuous view: in a sunny city square in Persia hung with colorful banners and flowers: happy people sing, dance in a circle, play tambourines and share baskets of food and gifts, children waving ribbons, while Queen Esther and Mordecai in blue-and-white royal robes wave from a palace balcony right of center

questions: Esther was scared, but she was brave anyway. What is something brave you could do?
Mordecai said maybe God made Esther queen “for such a time as this.” What good thing might God have made you for?
Esther asked her friends to pray before she did something hard. Who could you ask to pray for you?

verse.text: And who knows if perhaps you have come to the kingdom for such a time as this?
